comment: I dislike Bio 202, the course is unorganized so no matter who you take its gonna be difficult. Dr. Carrie is nice, but her grading is very harsh and she doesn't give partial credit. The way she words exam questions is overly complex and doesn't reflect your understanding of the material. Also, she wasn't clear with expectations for lab assignments.

I will be honest that while Dr. Carrie is so sweet and she is such a kind soul but when it comes to being a teacher I would not recommend her. Grades hard and takes off excessive points when the material she provides/teaches is unsubstantial. I had to email her multiple times before getting a response.

Dr. Carrie is approachable, authentic, and wants her students to succeed. While the workload was not trivial during my first semester at UR, now that I'm several semesters into the Bio major, I see SO MANY ways her course has prepared me for other classes! She was always available to help when I had questions. Definitely recommend her to anyone.
Her grading criteria is super unclear and the class is super disorganized and makes it really hard to study anything that will actually show up on the exam

Her grading criteria is unclear and her tests are super hard for no reason at all. She's a nice person but as a professor, she's just not for everyone. She talks super fast and will only talk about the things that she's passionate about even if it has to do nothing with the description of the class. If you are passionate about plants, take her.

Dr. Carrie integrates a lot of real-world issues into her class and makes that part of the labwork very rewarding. Her lectures are sometimes a little drawn out but she gives many examples of the course material.

Dr. Carrie truly cares about her students. She was always willing to answer my questions, and I really appreciated the time she took to give me constructive feedback on my lab write-ups. Her "Invasions in Biology" course focuses primarily on application over sheer memorization, which I found to be extremely helpful. Absolutely take her if you can!

Truly loved this course! Frequently integrated real-world subject matter into our coursework. Really cool that the lab taught so many skills, while also directly helping VA-DCR manage their preserves. The structure and assignments were also so fair- something that can't be said for all classes.

Dr. Carrie really cares about her students. I really liked the lab portion of this class, it was a lot more laid back than I expected. Lectures are example-heavy, so most tests and assignments are application based. Lots of little worksheets and assignments.

So so so so so nice. Sometimes its unclear how much each thing is worth, and whats graded versus what isn't but shes really nice and a good teacher. Sometimes lectures did get a little boring and repetitive tho

Dr Carrie is an amazing professor! I enjoyed her class and learned a lot. Her lecture style is engaging and she assigns interesting projects. I will definitely try to take another class with Dr. Carrie

Dr. Carrie is so so fun and uses a lot of detailed examples and demonstrations to explain concepts. She frequently has everyone get up and move around and work in groups to test our knowledge of the concepts and material. She grades very fairly and always gives very clear instructions on assignments.

Dr. Carrie is AMAZING. She care about her students inside and outside of class -- she is truly a genuine gem here at UR. Her class is pretty easy, tests are more "application-based," but very easy if you take notes during lecture and understand general concepts she emphasizes (more research-y side of biology). Class is not super technical.
She genuinely cares for her students
She's a gem

LOVE Dr. Carrie, she's seriously the best. Definitely a challenging class but very rewarding, she truly wants you to learn the basics of science so you can succeed in other classes. A few tests, lab reports on major labs, and two big presentations. She's very caring and accessible. She brought treats to  which was pretty awesome. Highly recommend!

This class was the hardest class I have ever taken in my life. Even though I got an A, my life was drained, soul, and will was pushed to the breaking point. Dr. Carrie is cool but her expectations are too much for a freshmen Bio class. Super easy to get a B but insanely hard to get an A.

Dr. Carrie made the "Invasions in Biology" class fun and engaging. Although the biology content is not heavy you really do learn how to "do" biology. Throughout the course, you get the chance to explore the tools biologists use and learn some things about field work. She is always open to help anyone that approaches her, even if it not about class.
Great class.  You need to keep up with the work, but lots of feedback.

Carrie cares about equipping her BIO199 students with the skills that are important for science majors (pipetting, learning how to interpret primary literature, learning how to write lab reports and convey data in figures, etc.). Expect homework regularly.

Dr. Carrie is a great professor and the "Invasions in Biology" section of BIOL 199 is amazing! Dr. Carrie is so nice and lots of fun to work with in class. She assigns a lot of small assignments, but these can help boost your grade if you take them seriously. She and her husband, Dr. Eugene, team-taught the class, and it was a great time!

I love Dr. Carrie. Not a fan of the mandatory field trip but she is so kind and friendly and truly wants you to learn. She is always there to help you if you need it however assignments are graded somewhat harshly so be thorough.

Dr. Carrie is really nice, and I enjoyed having her for lab this semester. The experiments rarely went according to plan, but we rolled with the punches and had fun. Assignments are not too bad, and the grading is fair. Overall a great professor, and an even better person. Would recommend for any bio class, not just evolution lab.
Dr. Wu is a really nice Professor. She really loves biology and it definitely shows. She is really helpful and lecture is always a lot of fun!

Great teacher, always willing to help. Does notes through powerpoint and posts those too. Tests are heavily based on scientific literature, but not too hard. Expectations are always clear. Overall great teacher, I would take her again in a heartbeat!
